title: Transportation Engineering
intro: Concise Notes for Competitive Exams — Extended Edition (lectures + online material, diagrams, MCQs & links)
Master handbook covering: Transportation Engineering + Exam Practice Pack
Overlapping topics have been merged into one chapter and repeated points removed. Practice MCQs for all parts are near the end; the answer key is the last chapter.

b: Transportation modes: Road, Rail, Air, Water, Pipeline. Road = most flexible, door-to-door service.
Jayakar Committee (1927): led to Central Road Fund (1929), IRC (1934), CRRI (1950).
Nagpur Plan (1943–63): 1st 20-yr plan; star & grid pattern; target 16 km/100 km² area.
Lucknow Plan (1981–2001): 3rd plan; 82 km/100 km²; village within 3 km of all-weather road.
Road classes (Nagpur): NH, SH, MDR, ODR, VR. Urban: Arterial, Sub-arterial, Collector, Local.
Road patterns: Rectangular/Grid (Chandigarh), Radial/Star, Hexagonal, Minimum travel (Nagpur pattern).
Pakistan: NHA (1991) manages national highways & motorways; M-2 Lahore–Islamabad = 1st motorway (1997).
Saturation system: road plan based on max utility per unit length (population + productivity served).
Highway alignment: should be short, easy, safe, economical. Factors: obligatory points, traffic, geometrics, economy.
Engineering surveys (order): Map study → Reconnaissance → Preliminary survey → Final location & detailed survey.
Extended material (beyond the lectures — standard textbooks & online sources)
Pakistan road network: National Highway Authority (NHA, 1991) maintains national highways (N-5 Karachi–Torkham is the longest, ≈ 1,800 km) and motorways (M-series).

Motorways: M-2 Lahore–Islamabad (1997) was the first motorway in South Asia; M-1 Islamabad–Peshawar; M-4 Pindi Bhattian–Multan; M-5 Multan–Sukkur; M-9 Karachi–Hyderabad; Hazara Motorway E-35 (CPEC route).
Provincial agencies: C&W (Communication & Works) Departments build and maintain provincial roads; KP Highways Authority; Punjab Highway Department.
Design practice in Pakistan: NHA largely follows AASHTO standards (AASHTO 1993 pavement design, AASHTO geometric design) alongside local specifications; IRC values are common in MCQ books.
Survey order: map study → reconnaissance → preliminary survey → final location & detailed survey.
Camber: transverse slope for drainage. Shapes: parabolic, straight line, combined.
Carriageway width (IRC): single lane 3.75 m; two lane 7.0 m; multilane 3.5 m per lane.
Max vehicle dimensions (IRC): width 2.5 m, height 3.8 m (4.2 m double-decker), length 11 m (single unit).
Shoulder: min 2.5 m (IRC). Kerb types: low/mountable (~10 cm), semi-barrier (~15 cm), barrier (~20 cm).
Right of way (ROW): land acquired; Formation width = carriageway + shoulders; Building line & control line set back.
Skid resistance: coefficient of longitudinal friction f = 0.35–0.40; lateral friction f = 0.15 (IRC).
Stopping Sight Distance (SSD) = lag distance + braking distance = 0.278 V t + V²/(254 f)  [V in km/h, t = 2.5 s, result in m].
With gradient: SSD = 0.278 V t + V²/[254 (f ± 0.01n)]; + for ascending, − for descending.
Overtaking Sight Distance (OSD) = d1 + d2 + d3 = 0.278 Vb t + (0.278 Vb T + 2s) + 0.278 V T.
OSD terms: t = 2 s reaction; s = 0.7 Vb + 6 (m); T = √(4s/a); Vb = V − 16 km/h (if not given).
Overtaking zone min length = 3 × OSD; desirable = 5 × OSD.
Eye height 1.2 m; object height 0.15 m (SSD), 1.2 m (OSD).
Perception–reaction time (PIEV): Perception, Intellection, Emotion, Volition; total 2.5 s for SSD.
Superelevation: e + f = V²/(127 R) [V km/h, R m].
IRC design: e = (0.75V)²/(127R) (75% speed, f neglected); max e = 7% (plains/rolling), 10% (hilly, non-snow), 4% urban with frequent intersections.
Overturning vs skidding: overturning if f > b/2h (rare); skidding governs when f < b/2h.
Methods of attaining superelevation: rotation about centre line, inner edge, or outer edge.
Extra widening: We = mechanical + psychological = n l²/(2R) + V/(9.5 √R) [n lanes, l wheelbase].
Transition curve: ideal shape = spiral (clothoid) — IRC recommends; lemniscate, cubic parabola also used.

Length of transition (IRC, max of 3 criteria): (1) rate of change of centrifugal acceleration Ls = 0.0215 V³/(C R), C = 80/(75+V), 0.5 ≤ C ≤ 0.8; (2) rate of superelevation; (3) empirical Ls = 2.7 V²/R (plain), V²/R (hilly).
Set-back distance (curve sight): m = R − (R − d) cos(θ/2); θ/2 = S/[2(R − d)] radians, for L > S.
Minimum gradient for drainage: 1 in 500 (concrete-lined drains); 1 in 200 (kutcha drains).
Grade compensation on curves = (30 + R)/R %, max 75/R %; not needed below 4%.
Vertical curve shape: square parabola (uniform rate of change of grade).
Summit curve (L > S): L = N S²/4.4 (SSD); L = N S²/9.6 (OSD). N = deviation angle = |n1 − n2|.
Valley curve: designed for comfort (centrifugal acceleration ≤ 0.6 m/s³) and headlight sight distance.
Valley curve comfort: L = 2 √(N V³/C) (V in m/s); headlight (L > S): L = N S²/(1.5 + 0.035 S).
Extended material (beyond the lectures — standard textbooks & online sources)
Fig. 2.1 — Cross-section elements: carriageway, camber, shoulders, formation width, right of way, side slopes.
Fig. 2.2 — SSD = lag distance (perception–reaction) + braking distance.
Fig. 2.3 — Forces on a vehicle on a superelevated curve.
Fig. 2.4 — Tangent → spiral transition → circular curve → spiral → tangent.
Fig. 2.5 — Summit (crest) and valley (sag) vertical curves.
Given: V = 80 km/h, t = 2.5 s, f = 0.35, level road.
Max superelevation (IRC): 7% plain & rolling, 10% hill roads (not snow-bound); min = camber. Max f for design = 0.15.
3 Es of traffic: Engineering, Enforcement, Education (+ Environment, Emergency).
Traffic studies: volume, speed (spot & journey), O–D, flow characteristics, parking, accident.
Spot speed: radar gun, enoscope (mirror box), pressure tubes. Journey speed: moving car (floating car) method.

Geometric design speed = 98th percentile speed (IRC); safe/upper speed limit for regulation = 85th percentile; lower speed limit = 15th percentile. (AASHTO practice also uses the 85th percentile as operating speed.)
O–D survey methods: road-side interview, licence plate, home interview, return post card, tag on car.
PCU (Passenger Car Unit): car = 1, bus/truck = 3, motorcycle = 0.5, cycle = 0.5, bullock cart = 8 (IRC values vary with speed).
AADT = annual average daily traffic; 30th highest hourly volume used as Design Hourly Volume (DHV).
Peak Hour Factor (PHF) = hourly volume / (4 × peak 15-min volume) ≤ 1.
Fundamental relation: q = k × v (flow = density × speed).
Greenshields model: v = vf (1 − k/kj); max flow qmax = vf kj / 4 at v = vf/2, k = kj/2.
Theoretical capacity C = 1000 V / S  (veh/h/lane), S = spacing in m = SSD + vehicle length.
Level of Service (HCM): A (free flow) to F (forced/breakdown flow).
STOP sign: octagonal, red; GIVE WAY: inverted triangle.
Road markings: white generally; yellow = no parking/no overtaking restrictions.
Intersections: at-grade (unchannelized, channelized, rotary, signalised) and grade-separated (interchange).
Conflict points, 4-legged intersection (two-way roads): 16 crossing (major) + 8 merging + 8 diverging = 32 total.
Rotary: design speed 40 km/h (rural), 30 km/h (urban); suitable traffic 500–3000 veh/h; weaving length 45–90 m (rural), 30–60 m (urban).
Rotary capacity (Wardrop): Qp = 280 w (1 + e/w)(1 − p/3) / (1 + w/L).
Signal types: fixed-time, vehicle-actuated, traffic-actuated, coordinated (simultaneous, alternate, flexible progressive).
Webster optimum cycle: Co = (1.5L + 5)/(1 − Y); L = total lost time, Y = Σ (critical q/s).
Amber time: 2–4 s (clearance). Pedestrian green ≥ crossing width / walking speed (≈1.2 m/s).
90° parking: max vehicles per kerb length; parallel: min; 45° accepted best compromise for accidents.
Parking studies: in–out survey, licence plate (patrol) method. Parking index = (occupied bays / total bays) × 100.
Accident studies: collision diagram & condition diagram; spot maps; accident rate per 100 million veh-km.
Accident rate R = (A × 10⁸) / (365 × T × V × L).
Extended material (beyond the lectures — standard textbooks & online sources)
Fig. 3.1 — Greenshields’ model: speed–density, flow–density and speed–flow relations.
Given: Two phases, critical flow ratios y₁ = 0.30, y₂ = 0.25; lost time per phase 2 s + all-red 4 s → L = 8 s.
Greens: Effective green = Co − L = 32 s → g₁ = 0.30/0.55 × 32 ≈ 17 s, g₂ ≈ 15 s.
Conflict points (4-leg, two-way): 32 total — 16 crossing, 8 merging, 8 diverging; rotary removes crossing conflicts.
Greenshields: maximum flow occurs at k = kj/2 and v = vf/2; qmax = vf·kj/4.
CBR test: penetration at 2.5 mm (standard load 1370 kg) and 5.0 mm (2055 kg); CBR = test load / standard load × 100.
Use higher CBR; if 5 mm value higher, repeat test — if still higher, adopt it.
Plate bearing test: modulus of subgrade reaction K = p / 0.125 cm (for 75 cm plate); correction for plate size & soaking.
Flaky: least dimension < 0.6 × mean size. Elongated: greatest dimension > 1.8 × mean size.
Los Angeles test is preferred for abrasion; simulates field wear (abrasive charge: steel balls).
Bitumen: petroleum product, soluble in CS₂. Tar: from destructive distillation of coal/wood, soluble in toluene.
Cutback = bitumen + volatile solvent: RC (rapid, gasoline/naphtha), MC (medium, kerosene), SC (slow, oil).
Emulsion = bitumen + water + emulsifier; RS (rapid), MS, SS. Cationic preferred for wet aggregates.
Modified bitumen: polymer (SBS, EVA), crumb rubber (CRMB) — better temperature susceptibility.
Needle 100 g, 5 s, 25°C; unit 0.1 mm; 80/100 grade
Viscosity grading (VG-10, 20, 30, 40) now replacing penetration grading; VG-30 most common.
Marshall method: specimen 101.6 mm dia × 63.5 mm; compaction 75 blows each face (heavy traffic), 50 blows (medium).
Marshall test at 60°C, loading 50.8 mm/min; outputs stability (kN) & flow value (0.25 mm units).
Volumetrics: Gm (bulk), Gt (theoretical), Vv air voids 3–5%, VMA = Vv + Vb, VFB = Vb/VMA × 100.
Optimum bitumen content = average of bitumen contents at max stability, max density, and 4% air voids.
Extended material (beyond the lectures — standard textbooks & online sources)

Bitumen tests: Penetration (hardness; 100 g, 5 s, 25 °C, units of 0.1 mm), ductility (cm at 27 °C), softening point (ring & ball), flash & fire point (safety), viscosity, specific gravity, loss on heating, solubility (CS₂/trichloroethylene).
Penetration grades: 80/100 (softer, cold areas), 60/70 (common in Pakistan’s hot plains), 40/50 (very hot areas, heavy traffic).

Aggregate tests: Crushing value (strength), Los Angeles abrasion (hardness), impact value (toughness), soundness (durability, Na₂SO₄/MgSO₄), shape (flakiness/elongation), stripping value (bitumen adhesion), specific gravity & water absorption.
Marshall criteria (typical): Stability ≥ 8–9 kN, flow 2–4 mm, air voids 3–5%, VMA ≥ 13–15%, VFB 65–75%.
Bitumen is soluble in CS₂; tar is obtained by destructive distillation of coal/wood. Cutbacks: RC (naphtha/gasoline), MC (kerosene), SC (oil).
Flexible: load transferred by grain-to-grain contact; layers — subgrade, sub-base, base, binder, surface (wearing) course.
Rigid: slab action (flexural strength); PCC slab on base/subgrade.
Semi-rigid: lean concrete / soil-cement bases; composite: flexible over rigid.
Methods: Empirical (CBR, Group Index, California resistance), Semi-empirical (Triaxial – Kansas), Theoretical (Burmister layered system).
IRC:37 — based on CBR & cumulative standard axles (msa); mechanistic-empirical (latest IRC:37-2018).
Standard axle load: 80 kN (8.16 t) single axle dual wheel.
Fourth power law (VDF): damage factor = (axle load / standard axle)⁴.
Cumulative standard axles: N = 365 A [(1+r)ⁿ − 1] × D × F / r; r = growth rate, D = lane distribution, F = VDF.
Lane distribution factor (IRC:37): single lane 1.0; two-lane single carriageway 0.5; four-lane single carriageway 0.4; dual carriageway — 2-lane 0.75, 3-lane 0.6, 4-lane 0.45.
ESWL (equivalent single wheel load): by equal stress (Boyd & Foster) or equal deflection criterion.
Critical strains: horizontal tensile strain at bottom of bituminous layer (fatigue cracking); vertical compressive strain on subgrade (rutting).
Burmister: Δ = 1.5 p a F / E (two-layer system).
Boussinesq (single layer, flexible plate): Δ = 1.5 p a / E; rigid plate: 1.18 p a / E.
Westergaard: stresses at interior, edge, corner. Edge = critical (wheel load); corner = highest at night (warping).
Radius of relative stiffness: l = [E h³ / (12 K (1 − μ²))]^0.25.
Equivalent radius of resisting section: b = √(1.6a² + h²) − 0.675h if a < 1.724h; b = a otherwise.
Warping (temperature) stress: Ste = (E α t / 2) × C (Bradbury coefficient).
Critical combination: day — edge load + warping (bottom tension); night — corner load + warping (top tension).
Frictional stress Sf = W Lc f / (2 × 10⁴)  (W = unit wt of concrete).
Joints: Expansion (dowel bars, 20–25 mm gap), Contraction (spacing 4.5 m), Construction, Warping/hinge.
Dowel bars: load transfer across transverse joints (plain round). Tie bars: hold longitudinal joints (deformed bars, not load transfer).
Concrete flexural strength ≥ 4.5 MPa (M40 typical); IRC:58 governs design.
Flexible failures: alligator/fatigue cracking, rutting, shoving, corrugation, bleeding, ravelling, potholes, reflection cracking.
Rigid failures: scaling, joint spalling, faulting, pumping, warping cracks, shrinkage cracks, D-cracking.
Benkelman beam: measures rebound deflection of flexible pavement → overlay design.
Bump integrator: measures surface unevenness (roughness, mm/km). Good surface < 2000 mm/km.
Overlay types: flexible over flexible, flexible over rigid, rigid over flexible, rigid over rigid.
Extended material (beyond the lectures — standard textbooks & online sources)
Fig. 5.1 — Layers of flexible and rigid pavements.
Given: A = 2000 CVPD, r = 7.5%, design life 15 years, VDF = 3.5, lane distribution D = 0.75.
AASHTO 1993 (NHA): Structural number SN = a₁D₁ + a₂D₂m₂ + a₃D₃m₃ (layer coefficients, thicknesses, drainage coefficients).
Fourth-power law: Doubling axle load increases damage ≈ 16 times — overloading is the main cause of premature failure on Pakistani highways.
Flexible pavement critical strains: horizontal tensile at bottom of bituminous layer (fatigue) and vertical compressive on top of subgrade (rutting).
WBM (water-bound macadam): stone aggregate + screenings + binding material, rolled with water.
WMM (wet mix macadam): premixed graded aggregate + water; better than WBM.
Prime coat: low-viscosity bitumen on porous (granular) surface. Tack coat: bitumen on existing bituminous/concrete surface for bonding.
Seal coat: top layer to make surface impervious. Surface dressing: bitumen + chips.
Bituminous layers: BM (bituminous macadam), DBM (dense bituminous macadam), BC (bituminous concrete — wearing), SDBC, Mastic asphalt.
Mastic asphalt: no rolling required; used on bridge decks.
Earthwork compaction: smooth-wheeled roller (granular, bituminous), sheep-foot (cohesive soils), pneumatic-tyred (mixed), vibratory (granular).
Surface drainage: camber, side drains, catch water drains (hill roads, uphill side).
Sub-surface drainage: lowering water table (longitudinal drains), intercepting seepage, control of capillary rise (capillary cut-off).
Rational formula for runoff: Q = C I A / 360 (Q m³/s, I mm/h, A hectares).
Hill roads: hair-pin bends (min radius 14–15 m), retaining walls (valley side), breast walls (hill side), catch water drains.
Extended material (beyond the lectures — standard textbooks & online sources)
Tack coat: Thin bitumen emulsion layer between two bituminous layers (bond).
Surface dressing: Single/double coat of bitumen + chips — cheap seal for low-traffic roads.
Hill-road drainage: Catch-water drains above the road, side drains on the hill side, cross drains (culverts), breast walls & retaining walls.
Culverts: Pipe culvert, box culvert, slab culvert, arch culvert — span up to ≈ 6 m (bridge if more).
Prime coat: on porous granular base; tack coat: on existing bituminous/impervious surface; seal coat: top impervious layer.
Permanent way: rails, sleepers, ballast, formation (subgrade) + fixtures/fastenings.
Rail types: double-headed, bull-headed, flat-footed (Vignoles) — most used.
Rail length: 12.8 m (42 ft) BG; 11.89 m (39 ft) MG. Long welded rails (LWR) reduce joints.
Coning of wheels: slope 1 in 20; prevents wheel flange rubbing & keeps vehicle central. Rails tilted inward at 1 in 20 (adzing of sleepers).
Creep: longitudinal movement of rails. Measured by creep indicator; prevented by anchors/creep anchors.
Wear of rails max on outer rail on curves; side wear.
Sleeper density = n + x (n = rail length in m); e.g., M + 7 for BG main lines.
Sleeper types: wooden (best elasticity), steel, cast iron, concrete (prestressed, most used now).
Ballast: broken stone (best), size 50 mm for BG; functions — load distribution, drainage, elasticity.
Fish plates: join rails at ends. Expansion gap provided for temperature.
Equilibrium cant: e = G V² / (127 R) (G gauge in mm, V km/h, R m) → e in mm.
Max cant: BG 165 mm (185 mm for special); MG 100 mm.
Cant deficiency: BG 75 mm (100 mm high-speed); MG 50 mm.
Negative cant: on the turnout branch curve opposite to main line curve.
Degree of curve: D = 1750 / R (30.5 m chord); D = 1146 / R (20 m chord).
Max permissible speed (BG, transitioned curve): V = 0.27 √[(Ca + Cd) R]  (Ca, Cd in mm).
Transition length = max of 0.008 Ca Vm, 0.008 Cd Vm, 0.72 Ca.
Grade compensation on curves: BG 0.04% per degree; MG 0.03%; NG 0.02%.
Ruling gradient: 1 in 150–200 (plains), 1 in 100 (hilly). Momentum & pusher gradients steeper.
Gradient at stations (yards): max 1 in 400 (prevent runaway); min 1 in 1000 for drainage.
Turnout components: points (switches), lead rails, crossing (frog), check rails, heel block.
Number of crossing N = cot α; methods: right-angle (Cole's), centre-line, isosceles triangle.
Switch angle: angle between stock rail and tongue rail.
Track junctions: diamond crossing, scissors crossover, gauntlet track, triangle (to reverse direction of engine).
Signals: semaphore, colour light; absolute block system ensures one train per block section.
Station yards: marshalling yard (sorting wagons, hump yard), loco yard, goods yard, passenger yard.
Hauling capacity of locomotive = μ × W × n (μ coefficient of adhesion ≈ 0.2 dry rail).
Train resistances: due to friction, wave action, speed, wind, gradient, curvature, starting/accelerating.
Extended material (beyond the lectures — standard textbooks & online sources)
Fig. 7.1 — Permanent way: rails, fastenings, sleepers, ballast and formation.
Fig. 7.2 — Turnout: stock rail, tongue rails, lead rails, crossing (frog), check and wing rails.
Pakistan Railways: Mostly broad gauge (1676 mm); ML-1 (Karachi–Peshawar, ≈ 1,726 km) is the main line planned for upgrading under CPEC; ML-2 and ML-3 are other main lines.
Rail weight: Expressed in kg/m (e.g., 52 kg/m, 60 kg/m UIC rails); older in lb/yd.
Long welded rails: Reduce joints, noise and maintenance; need de-stressing and good ballast.
Coning of wheels 1 in 20; equilibrium cant e = GV²/(127R); max cant BG 165 mm; cant deficiency BG 75 mm.
Airport site factors: regional plan, airspace, surrounding obstructions, ground accessibility, meteorology, soil, noise, future expansion.
Runway orientation: along prevailing wind; determined by wind rose diagram (Type I: direction & duration; Type II: direction, duration & intensity).
Crosswind component: max 25 km/h (large aircraft), 15 km/h (small); runway coverage ≥ 95% (ICAO).
Basic runway length: at sea level, 15°C, zero gradient, no wind.
Corrections (ICAO): elevation +7% per 300 m; temperature +1% per 1°C above standard (T = Ta + (Tm − Ta)/3); gradient +20% per 1% effective gradient.
Combined elevation + temperature correction should not exceed 35%.
Standard atmosphere temperature drops 6.5°C per km altitude.
Taxiway: connects runway to apron/terminal; exit taxiway (high-speed) angle 30° (ideal), 45°.
Apron: aircraft parking/loading area. Hangar: aircraft repair & housing.
Holding apron: near runway end for final checks before take-off.
Turning zone: provided at runway end when no parallel taxiway.
Clearway: obstacle-free area beyond runway. Stopway: paved area beyond runway for aborted take-off.
Imaginary surfaces (obstruction clearance): approach, transitional, inner horizontal (45 m height), conical.
Airport classification (ICAO aerodrome reference code): number 1–4 by field length; letter A–F by wingspan.
Lighting: approach lighting, runway edge lights (white), taxiway edge lights (blue), threshold lights (green), runway end (red).
ILS (instrument landing system): localiser (azimuth) + glide path + marker beacons.
Extended material (beyond the lectures — standard textbooks & online sources)
Fig. 8.1 — Airport elements: runway, taxiways, exit taxiway, apron, terminal, hangar, holding apron.
Runway numbering: Magnetic bearing ÷ 10, rounded (e.g., 087° → runway 09; opposite end 27).
Wind coverage: Runway oriented so that ≥ 95% of the time the crosswind component is within permissible limits (wind rose analysis).

Pakistan airports: Managed by Pakistan Airports Authority; main international airports — Islamabad (New Islamabad International Airport), Lahore (Allama Iqbal), Karachi (Jinnah), Peshawar (Bacha Khan).
Runway markings white; taxiway markings yellow; runway edge lights white; taxiway edge lights blue.
Harbour: sheltered area for ships. Types — natural, semi-natural, artificial.
Breakwater: protects harbour from waves (mound type, wall type, composite).
Wet dock: water level maintained by lock gates. Dry dock: for ship repair (emptied of water).
Jetty/pier: projects into water; wharf: parallel to shore; quay: wharf retaining land.
Fender: absorbs ship impact. Dolphin: mooring structure away from shore.
Tunnel shapes: circular (best for soft ground & water pressure), egg, horseshoe (rock), D-shape.
Tunnelling in soft ground: shield method, needle beam, liner plate; in rock: full face, heading & bench, drift method; TBM for both.
Extended material (beyond the lectures — standard textbooks & online sources)
Pakistan ports: Karachi Port, Port Qasim, Gwadar Port (deep-sea, CPEC).
Tunnel surveys: Alignment transferred through shafts; tunnels in Pakistan — Lowari, Kohat, Malakand, Attabad (KKH), Lahore Orange Line (cut-and-cover/elevated).
NATM: New Austrian Tunnelling Method — shotcrete + rock bolts, uses the ground’s own strength; widely used in rock tunnels.
Mound (rubble) breakwater for deep water/soft bed is costlier in material; wall-type breakwater needs a firm bed.
Stop / overtake (d₁ + d₂ + d₃) / intermediate = 2 × SSD
0.15 m for SSD; 1.2 m for OSD (oncoming car)
Sight distance, square parabola vs comfort & headlight, cubic parabola
Porous base vs existing bituminous surface
Grain-to-grain, CBR / slab action, K & Westergaard
Full-depth gap with dowels vs dummy groove (crack inducer)
Load transfer at transverse joints vs hold slabs at longitudinal joints
Longitudinal movement vs loss of metal (outer rail on curves)
Obstacle-free area for take-off climb vs paved area for stopping in aborted take-off
At-grade weaving vs grade-separated (trumpet, diamond, cloverleaf)
e + f = V²/(127R); IRC design e = (0.75V)²/(127R) ≤ 7% (plain), 10% (hill)
Comfort L = 2√(Nv³/C), C = 0.6 m/s³; headlight L = NS²/(1.5 + 0.035S)
q = kv; qmax = vf·kj/4; capacity C = 1000V/S
Load at 2.5 mm/1370 kg or at 5 mm/2055 kg × 100
e = GV²/(127R) (G ≈ 1750 mm for BG, between rail centres)
+7% per 300 m elevation; +1% per °C (ART − standard); +20% per 1% effective gradient; elev + temp ≤ 35%
V = 80 km/h, R = 250 m: C = 80/155 = 0.52; Ls = 0.0215 × 80³/(0.52 × 250) = 85 m (compare with empirical 2.7 × 80²/250 = 69 m and superelevation criterion; adopt the largest).

Basic length 2000 m; elevation 300 m; aerodrome reference temperature 30 °C; effective gradient 0.5%. Elevation: 2000 × 1.07 = 2140 m. Standard temp at 300 m = 15 − 0.0065 × 300 = 13.05 °C → +16.95% → 2503 m (combined +25% < 35% ✔). Gradient: × 1.10 → 2753 m.
A 10 t single axle: VDF = (10/8.16)⁴ = 2.26 standard axles — 23% heavier load does 2.26 times the damage.
